PullRequest.Title: Copilot: migrate embedding-backed features to Metis
PullRequest.Body:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

Migrates Copilot's embedding-backed features from text-embedding-3-small to Metis.

## Changes

- Select embedding endpoint metadata by model family and preserve Metis query/document input roles.
- Move API context, settings/commands lookup, project-template matching, and virtual-tool embeddings to Metis.
- Use model-scoped local caches and the lowercase Metis CDN prefix produced by the publishing pipeline.
- Support both the published array-shaped tool cache and the legacy object-shaped cache.
- Keep the generic `vscode.lm` embeddings provider on text3small because that API cannot express query/document roles.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The model dimensions, number-array representation, full-index retention, and component-wise ranking loop are explicit in the repository, so the 2x scaling mechanism is certain. Exact heap and latency magnitude depends on each installation's contributed setting/command count and engine representation, which is why severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Long-lived JavaScript number-array elements for every cached setting and command embedding, plus CPU work for their dot products
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Resident elements and dot-product iterations scale with the total settings and commands loaded from core and installed extensions; changing each vector from 512 to 1024 dimensions doubles both per-entry quantities.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased retained heap and CPU/GC pressure, with longer synchronous ranking work after each settings search or VS Code assistant query
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The settings and command caches and query embeddings used text3small_512, so each retained item had 512 numeric components and each distance calculation iterated 512 components.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed cache constructors load Metis 1024-dimensional vectors for both complete indexes, while BaseEmbeddingsIndex keeps every vector in its session-long maps and rankEmbeddings/distance scans every component of every indexed entry.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 294 replaces EmbeddingType.text3small_512 with EmbeddingType.metis_1024_I16_Binary for the complete settings cache; the adjacent changed command-cache line makes the same replacement, increasing retained vector width for all entries from 512 to 1024.
Findings.Title: Keep binary Metis index vectors compact
Findings.Impact: On installations with thousands of core and extension-contributed settings/commands, loading these indexes now retains twice as many JS numeric elements, and every settings-editor search or VS Code assistant lookup performs twice as many multiply-add iterations before returning ranked results.
Findings.Evidence: EmbeddingType metadata defines Metis at 1024 dimensions versus text3small at 512, and EmbeddingVector remains readonly number[]. RemoteEmbeddingsCache JSON-parses these arrays, BaseEmbeddingsIndex._calculateEmbeddings attaches them to every item in _items, and distance() loops to the vector length. The changed lines 294-298 migrate both all-settings and all-commands caches to Metis, while provideSettingsSearchResults and VscodePrompt synchronously rank the full loaded indexes on their response path.
Findings.Recommendation: Convert cached binary document embeddings to a compact representation (for example a bit-packed or Int8-backed vector) as they are loaded and make distance consume that representation, rather than retaining 1,024 boxed/JS-number components per entry; keep query/document semantics and ranking results unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Settings Editor semantic search and VS Code assistant settings/command lookup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A query must complete one remote embedding request, then on the first lookup load the command/settings indexes, and synchronously score/sort their retained entries before results progress. Optional LLM reranking occurs afterward. The diff doubles vector width on this critical path from 512 to 1024.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute the query embedding through Dotcom embeddings or CAPI embeddings
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the single query; for no-auth CAPI, one models request can additionally occur on a cold or older-than-10-minute metadata cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same query path made one text3small embedding request; the diff changes model family and payload role, not request count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks ranking and all embedding-based results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two IPC calls on cold index initialization, one per complete collection, in parallel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two collection-wide IPC calls initialized the text3small indexes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks first index construction; absent after the in-memory indexes are loaded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch CDN latest/core files and missing installed-extension embedding files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold: two latest checks, up to two core downloads, and up to two requests per installed non-VS-Code extension (one settings and one commands cache); per-index extension requests are sequential. Warm in-memory indexes make zero calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cold-cache fan-out existed for text3small; the diff changes the container and local cache namespace because the embeddings are incompatible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read, clear, and persist the two model-scoped embedding caches
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one read and, when CDN state changed, one clear/write sequence per settings or command cache during cold initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operations used unscoped text3small filenames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks first index load; no index filesystem operations after in-memory load.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All core and installed-extension settings plus commands; effective ranking cardinality is the number of entries with embeddings, with no grouping or result-limit shortcut before scoring.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The command and settings index loads run in parallel via Promise.all. Within each index, extension CDN files are fetched sequentially. A one-input embedding request is one network call; CAPI batching is globally serial within that request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold index load checks each model-scoped disk cache and CDN latest marker, downloads core and missing per-extension caches, and persists them. Once BaseEmbeddingsIndex is loaded, later queries reuse its in-memory maps and do not reload the CDN/disk indexes; each query still requests a fresh query embedding. The new model key correctly prevents incompatible text3small reuse but retains twice as many numeric vector elements.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: dimensions, number-array retention, all-entry scoring, and changed model selection are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact entry counts, JS-engine element representation, and milliseconds vary by installed extensions, but thousands of settings/commands are realistic and the 2x component count is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the model migration materially amplifies long-lived numeric elements and full-index dot-product work by 2x; submitted as a medium memory/CPU regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: VS Code API context retrieval for extension-development chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The API cache update must finish, then one remote query embedding and a full API-chunk ranking must complete before prompt context is rendered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check/download the API embedding CDN cache
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One latest check per render and one core download per cache instance/version when cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same latest/core operations occurred against the text3small container.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read or persist the API embedding cache JSON
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per update and a clear/write sequence when the CDN version differs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same operations with the prior cache filename/model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the prompt critical path before query ranking.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per rendered API-context query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One text3small request was made at the same point.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All API/documentation chunks in the CDN cache; ranking scores every chunk before sorting and taking five.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cache update, embedding request, and ranking are sequential. The one-input embedding request is a single network call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold use checks latest, downloads the Metis API cache, and persists it. The RemoteEmbeddingsCache instance retains the downloaded object, but updateIndex still performs the pre-existing latest check on each render. The diff changes cache namespace/model and doubles vector component width.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for path and boundary counts; medium for exact memory/latency magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not expose the published API chunk count or endpoint latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same 1024-number retention/scoring amplification exists, but it is the same mechanism as the submitted full-index finding and was not duplicated.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Intent classification chat completes first; for project intent with templates enabled, one query embedding, first-use template cache load, full template ranking, then recursive GitHub repository content fetches must complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Classify new-workspace intent with the utility chat model
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks determining whether template search runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute the project description query embedding
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for project intent with templates enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One text3small embedding request occurred at the same point.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One latest check and at most one core download on first use per service lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same count against the text3small cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read or persist the project-template embedding cache
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold read and optional clear/write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same operations under the old cache key.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively list selected template repository contents
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the root and one additional request per nested directory, sequentially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks workspace metadata/result construction after a template is selected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One query, all template entries for ranking, then one GitHub contents request per directory reached in the selected template repository.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Intent, embedding, cache/ranking, and repository traversal are sequential. GitHub directory traversal is recursively serial. CAPI embedding batching has effective parallelism one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ProjectTemplatesIndex loads once per service lifetime. Cold use checks/downloads/persists the model-scoped CDN cache; warm use reuses the in-memory array. Query embeddings are never cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call ordering, cache behavior, and boundary multiplicity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Published template count and selected repository depth vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: model/cache target changes preserve boundary cardinality; vector-width amplification is covered by the submitted mechanism.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: On first use, precomputed CDN and local tool caches initialize; then a query embedding is fetched, embeddings for cache-missing available tools are computed in batches, and available tools are ranked/grouped before tool selection completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check/download precomputed tool embeddings from the CDN
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One latest check and at most one core download on lazy first use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same operations for the text3small precomputed cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the model-scoped CDN cache and binary local tool cache; persist runtime-computed tools after a scheduler delay
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local read on initialization; one deferred aggregate write after new entries, not on the immediate critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same lifecycle, with the old model cache becoming incompatible once due to migration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial read blocks first use; delayed save is off the request critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute query embedding and document embeddings for cache-missing tools
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query request plus ceil(missingTools/batchLimit) document requests; requests are serial.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request grouping and frequency using text3small; the diff supplies Metis roles/model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both block tool ranking when needed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Available extension/MCP tools after built-in filtering; missing tool documents are grouped into batches of 100 on Dotcom or endpoint max_inputs on CAPI, while ranking scales with available embedded tools.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Precomputed and local cache initialization run in parallel. Missing tools share one computeEmbeddings invocation; Dotcom sends batches sequentially and CAPI uses Limiter parallelism 1. Tool result waits are serialized by tool order but share the same batch promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The precomputed cache is loaded once through Lazy initialization. The local cache rejects the old embedding type and is repopulated for missing tools; later calls reuse precomputed/local/in-memory entries. CDN negative extension behavior is not involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for coalescing, batch cardinality, and cache lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Available and cache-missing tool counts differ substantially by extension/MCP configuration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: no new fan-out or concurrency burst; wider retained precomputed vectors share the reported allocation mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Related-information provider queries for settings and commands
Scenarios.CriticalPath: If an index is not loaded, calculation is started in the background and the request returns immediately. Once loaded, one remote query embedding blocks the request, followed by a synchronous scan/sort of all embedded items.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per loaded-index provider query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One text3small request was made at the same point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks results; cold-index requests avoid this by returning immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load all settings or all commands during background index construction
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One collection-wide IPC call per index initialization, coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the triggering cold request path, but required before later queries can return matches.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Every loaded setting or command entry with an embedding; result cap applies only after all scores are computed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold background index calculation is coalesced by _calculationPromise. Loaded-query scoring is single-threaded; one embedding network request is in flight per provider call, subject to caller cancellation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold calculation uses the same model-scoped remote extension caches as settings search. Loaded maps are reused for the service lifetime. Query embeddings are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the hot scan and changed 2x dimensionality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Invocation frequency is controlled by VS Code consumers and is not quantified in this repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: The doubled component-wise scan is covered by the submitted settings/command index finding; no separate boundary regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 16 changed files and traced embedding queries, cache loading, endpoint resolution, full-index ranking, tool initialization, and project-template lookup. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity finding for materially amplified retained vector storage and component-wise ranking work after moving full settings/command indexes from 512 to 1024 dimensions. Cache namespaces, endpoint selection, input roles, and array/object cache compatibility did not otherwise add reportable boundary counts or concurrency.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
